oliver: Quick heads-up from a new user run of the onboarding sample: when OpenTelemetry is toggled we get a lot of DEBUG network spam, some lines missing req_id, and at least one header leaked an email-like value.

Sasha: Can you paste the exact steps + a short log snippet?

oliver: Steps: `git checkout samples/onboard-guides && npm ci && TELEMETRY=on ./dev up` then `./dev logs`. Minimal snippet attached: 
```
2026-06-01T15:04:10.001Z INFO runner booted
2026-06-01T15:04:10.123Z DEBUG http.core request -> POST /v1/respond
2026-06-01T15:04:10.124Z DEBUG http.core raw-headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX user-email=frank@example.com
2026-06-01T15:04:10.125Z WARN telemetry req_id not present on outbound
```
oliver: Note Authorization token is redacted by our logger but `user-email` is visible. Also when I flip `TELEMETY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` I see more lines without req_id.

leo: Which SDK version does that sample pin? We changed the injector order in 0.9.x so older pins can mismatch with the new env toggles.

oliver: package.json shows `redwood-sdk@0.8.10`. I tried swapping to `redwood-sdk@^0.9.2` locally and saw fewer missing req_id lines.

Sasha: Short-term mitigation suggestions: set `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info` in the sample env so new users aren't swamped; add a defensive header-scrub in our lowest-level HTTP wrapper that normalizes header keys and redacts email/token/ip patterns before handing off to upstream libs; and add a CI integration that runs the sample with `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` to assert logs contain no PII.

leo: Also ensure req_id injection happens before any retry or network debug logging. We shipped `ensureReqId()` helper in SDK 0.9.1 that guarantees an id is available to early middleware; older SDKs lack that. For safety, the sample should either bump SDK or add a local shim that calls `ensureReqId()` early.

oliver: I tried the shim: calling `ensureReqId()` at the top of retry handler reduced the missing-id lines. But the raw header leak still happens because some network libs log internals before our wrapper runs.

Sasha: For those cases we can add a tiny normalization step at the HTTP primitive level (the single file that touches fetch/undici/undici polyfill). That function should run before we construct the actual request and before any param gets logged by the underlying lib. Keep it conservative: only redact when key name contains "user"/"email"/"auth" OR value matches common PII regex (email/token/ip). Default the strict scrub off behind `REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT=true` so we can ship fast.

leo: Add tests: unit tests that mock a low-level lib printing a header string and assert the captured logs contain `<redacted_email>` instead of the real email; CI integration job that runs sample twice (default + `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first`) and searches logs for email regexes — fail if any found. Also a test to ensure we don't double-redact (e.g., `Bearer <redacted_token>` appears only once).

sdk-bot: FYI related SDK PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/451 (ensureReqId helper) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/459 (header normalization docs).

ci-bot: CI queued for branch oliver/onboard-telemetry-scrub: lint, unit, logs-scan. :gear:

Sasha: Can you also add a one-liner in the quickstart: "If you see lots of DEBUG network logs or missing request ids on first run, set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info or bump the sample SDK to ^0.9.x"? New contributors keep filing the same tickets.

oliver: Yep, I'll add the README blurb and open a PR with (1) sample SDK bump, (2) small normalizeHeaders() in http primitive, (3) unit + integration logs-scan job, (4) README note. I'll default `REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT=false` and document how to opt-in for stricter scrub.

leo: Land the scrub behind a feature flag; prefer a gradual rollout. After PR lands I'll run a quick local e2e with `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` and aggressive retry to validate.

Sasha: Thanks — tagging docs & support in PR to add the quick triage bullet. Leaving my dev stack running to verify once CI green. :thumbsup:

oliver: Thanks team :tada:
